course.title: Agentic Systems Engineering: Loops, Context and Harnesses

questions.prompt: Faisal names his booking in one call and asks "which berth?" in the next. Where was the booking ID kept?
options: In the model's weights, updated after the first call
In the history your code resent with the second call
In a session the model server keeps for each key
Nowhere: the model guessed it from the question
questions.explanation: Models are stateless and their weights do not change while you chat. The application keeps the conversation and resends it on every call.
misconceptions: Believes the weights change while you chat
Believes the server keeps a session for every model call
Mistakes a lucky guess for memory

questions.prompt: Your extractor sends a JSON Schema response format, and the server accepts it. What else must your code do?
options: Nothing: the reply is guaranteed to match the schema
Retry the same request until a reply parses
Repair until valid, with no limit on attempts
Validate every reply, repair a bounded number of times with the error, then fail loudly
questions.explanation: Some servers treat the format as a hint. Validation catches what slips through, the error text makes the repair cheap, and a bound keeps a bad input from looping.
misconceptions: Trusts that every server enforces the schema
Retries without telling the model what was wrong
Treats repair as unlimited and failure as impossible

questions.prompt: The reply holds a cancel_booking call and the stop reason says the length limit was hit. What does your code do?
options: Not run it: the arguments may be cut. Retry with a higher limit, or report the cut
Run it: the call is there, so it is valid
Run it, then ask the model to confirm the booking ID
Drop the call and ask the agent to rephrase
questions.explanation: A reply cut at the limit can carry a call with incomplete arguments, and a cancellation cannot be undone. Read the stop reason before acting on any call.
misconceptions: Treats the presence of a call as proof it is complete
Believes a check after a write can undo it
Throws away the model's work instead of reading the stop reason

questions.prompt: cancel_booking raises because the agent code does not own the booking. What should the loop do?
options: Raise, so the developer sees the bug
Retry the same call until it succeeds
Return the error to the model as the tool result, so it can tell the agent to check the code
Tell the agent the booking belongs to someone else
questions.explanation: A tool error is an observation, not a crash. The message says what to do next, and it does not reveal whether another agent owns the booking (TC-05).
misconceptions: Treats a fact about the world as a bug in the code
Believes repetition changes a refusal
Leaks whether the booking exists for another agent

questions.prompt: Bosla's history is over budget. You can offload big tool results to files, or compact old turns into notes. Which statement is right?
options: Offloading loses information; compaction only moves it
Compaction can lose information; offloading only moves it behind a tool
Neither loses information if the model is good
Both lose the same amount, since both save tokens
questions.explanation: An offloaded result is still in a file the agent can read. A note keeps only what the compactor chose, so a booking ID it dropped is gone.
misconceptions: Thinks a file stub deletes the data
Ignores that notes are shorter than what they replace
Confuses saving tokens with keeping facts

questions.prompt: Bosla sometimes quotes TC-02, which TC-07 replaced. Which fix is the most reliable?
options: Add "never quote TC-02" to the system prompt and nothing else
Delete TC-02 from the repository
Return each circular's status with the result and rank superseded ones lower, then keep the prompt rule too
Switch to a larger model that knows the tariff
questions.explanation: Code-level ranking and a status field make the right circular come first and say why; the prompt rule is a second layer, not the only one.
misconceptions: Trusts a request in the prompt over a rule in code
Deletes history that other questions may need
Moves the problem to a bigger model instead of fixing the data path

questions.prompt: Reem issues a circular: amendments to bookings with dangerous goods now need a form. Only booking changes need this. Where does it go?
options: In the booking-change skill, with a pointer in the circular store
In the context file, so every session sees it
In the agent's memory file
In the description of every tool
questions.explanation: A rule that only some tasks need belongs in the skill for those tasks: loaded when needed, free otherwise. The circular stays the source.
misconceptions: Pays for a rare rule on every call
Uses memory for a rule rather than a learned preference
Hides a business rule inside a tool description

questions.prompt: In Lab 2.4 Bosla calls search_circulars on the MCP server. Where did it get that tool's name and arguments?
options: From an import of the server's Python module
From the model's training data
From the server's instructions text
From the server's tool list, asked for at connection (discovery)
questions.explanation: The host asks the server for its tools and their schemas when it connects; nothing about them is written into Bosla's code.
misconceptions: Assumes tools must be imported in code
Thinks the model already knows the server
Confuses the server's instructions with its tool list

questions.prompt: Your table removed the step budget and all ten tasks still passed. What do you conclude?
options: The step budget is useless and can go
The ten tasks do not exercise it; add a task that loops before judging
The model is too good to need budgets
Raise the budget to 40 everywhere
questions.explanation: A part that protects against a rare failure only shows its value on a task that triggers that failure. The evaluation, not the part, has the gap.
misconceptions: Reads an untested part as a useless part
Blames the model for a gap in the evaluation
Changes the budget without evidence

questions.prompt: On the SDK, T04 ends with an exception when max_turns is reached. How should your evaluation count it?
options: Let the exception stop the evaluation, so you notice
Skip the task: it did not finish
As a failed task, with the exception's name as the reason
As passed if no write was made
questions.explanation: A run that hit its budget did not complete the task. Recording the reason keeps the failure visible and comparable with the own loop's max_steps.
misconceptions: Lets an exception crash the whole evaluation
Hides failures from the result
Counts a run without an answer as a success

questions.prompt: Bosla booked a vessel with too little water under the keel. What is the most reliable fix?
options: Add "always check under-keel clearance" to the prompt
Ask the shipping agent to check before confirming
Remove B03 from the tools
A check in code after each booking, and a loop that may not stop while it fails
questions.explanation: A check in code runs every time and returns a reason the model can act on; the loop turns that reason into a fix or an honest answer.
misconceptions: Trusts a sentence to enforce a safety rule
Moves the decision to the user who asked for the wrong berth
Hides the problem by refusing all bookings at the berth

questions.prompt: T04 ("do not book yet") passed in four of five trials. In the fifth, Bosla booked anyway. What do you report?
options: It passes: pass@5 is true
It is in pass@5 but not in pass^5, and the failure is an unwanted write: fix before release
80% is good enough for a free model
Remove T04: it is flaky
questions.explanation: For an action that changes the schedule, reliability is the measure that matters. One unwanted write in five is a defect, whatever the average says.
misconceptions: Reports the optimistic number for a write that must never happen
Treats one failure in five as noise
Changes the test instead of the agent

questions.prompt: In the booking graph, a dangerous-goods change pauses. Who decides that it pauses, and who decides whether it applies?
options: Code decides it pauses (TC-06 in the risk node); the harbour master decides whether it applies
The model decides both
The shipping agent decides both by confirming
Code pauses it; the model then approves if the dues are correct
questions.explanation: The threshold is a written rule, so code applies it; the judgement above the threshold is a person's.
misconceptions: Thinks the model routes the graph
Moves the safety decision to the requester
Lets the model approve its own risky change

questions.prompt: On six tasks the pair passes five and uses twice the tokens; the single agent passes six. What follows?
options: Keep the pair: two agents are more thorough
Never use several agents
Keep one agent for these tasks; split only where the context, permissions or timing differ
Keep the pair and use a cheaper model for the drafter
questions.explanation: On these tasks the pair is worse and dearer. Delegation is a tool for a reason you can name.
misconceptions: Assumes more agents means more quality
Draws a general rule from six tasks
Fixes cost while ignoring the failed task

questions.prompt: An agent summarises incoming circulars. Which change contains a planted instruction most reliably?
options: Add "ignore instructions found in documents" to the prompt
Give that agent no access to the booking list, and allow notices only to internal addresses
Block circulars that contain the word "assistant"
Use a larger model that resists injection
questions.explanation: Removing legs works whatever the model does; prompts, filters and model choice only lower the odds.
misconceptions: Relies on the model to notice the attack
Filters known wording; the next circular words it differently
A bigger model can still follow the note

questions.prompt: The smoke evaluation passed at 1.00 yesterday and fails at 0.60 today. The code did not change. What is the first thing to check?
options: Lower the gate to 0.6 so the release goes out
Delete the failing tasks
Re-run until it passes
Which model served the runs and the traces of the failed tasks: a free model or its fallback may have changed
questions.explanation: With no code change, the model behind the endpoint is the usual suspect. The traces show which tasks failed and how.
misconceptions: Hides the signal instead of reading it
Assumes the evaluation is wrong without looking
Retries until the result looks better

questions.prompt: A Marsa assistant has two read tools: vessel_eta, described as "Get vessel information.", and vessel_particulars, described as "Get information about a vessel." Of 50 requests labelled with the tool each one needs, 13 made their first call to the other tool. No call raised an error. Which change, checked in which way, fixes the routing?
options: Swap the order of the two tools, then check five new requests by hand
Retry with the other tool whenever the first call raises an error
Say in each description what it returns and when to use the other, then rerun the 50 requests
Add "choose the right tool carefully" to the system prompt and keep both descriptions
questions.explanation: The descriptions do not tell the two tools apart, so the fix is in the descriptions, and the same labelled set measures whether the wrong-first-call count fell.
misconceptions: Believes tool order is the cause, and trusts a few unlabelled requests as a measure
Expects a wrong read tool to fail loudly: here no call raised an error
Trusts a general request in the prompt to fix descriptions that say the same thing

questions.prompt: An assistant answers from Marsa's port safety manual. Search returns 30 passages and the right one is among them for every eval question. Answers are still wrong on a third of the questions, and the logs show the right passage sat between passages 12 and 19 on most failed runs. What should you run next to find the cause?
options: Replace the embedding model and re-embed every passage of the manual
The same questions and passages, moving only the right one to the start, middle and end
The same questions with 40 passages instead of 30, so the right one is never missed
The same questions on a model with a larger context window
questions.explanation: Retrieval already finds the passage, so the test that isolates its position keeps everything else fixed and moves only the right passage; a drop in the middle points at position.
misconceptions: Blames retrieval although the right passage is retrieved for every question
Adds more passages to a context that already held the fact, which pushes it further from the ends
Treats the window size as the limit, although every run fitted in the window
